lines.text: Software for running a call for papers has always been sold the same way.
This is Trackstage. Call for papers, agenda, and speaker management — in one fast, simple, open-source tool.
You build the form yourself — every question, every track.
Speakers apply in minutes, straight from a link. No account to create, no password to remember.
Review everything in one place, and stage your decisions — nothing sends by accident.
When you're sure, commit the queue — and every email goes out at once.
Every speaker gets their own portal — submissions, profile, and tasks.
Then drag the agenda together — rooms, tracks and time slots, with conflicts caught live.
Or let auto-place schedule the rest for you.
Publish when you're ready — a clean public schedule, with calendar invites included.
There's an AI copilot built in. Ask it to run your event — it always checks with you first.
Or drive the whole thing from Claude, ChatGPT, or Codex.
And when your program is ready, embed it on your own website.
Free, open source, and live right now.
The whole product is MIT licensed. Self-host it, or use the cloud beta — for exactly nothing.
Trackstage. Ready to open your call for papers? It's waiting at trackstage dot app.
